In two sentences, describe what makes a memory-bound program different from a compute-bound one.

local.text: A memory-bound program is limited by the speed at which data can be accessed from memory, often due to frequent cache misses or slow memory bandwidth. In contrast, a compute-bound program is constrained by the processing speed of the CPU, as it spends most of its time performing calculations rather than waiting for data.
